impTopics.title: Operating System Concepts: Memory Management and Multitasking Fundamentals
impTopics.description: In a multiprogrammed system, multiple jobs are kept in memory, with one job selected and run through job scheduling. If a job has to wait, the operating system switches to another job, enabling timesharing or multitasking where the CPU switches between jobs frequently to allow user interaction. CPU scheduling is used when multiple jobs are ready to run simultaneously, and swapping and virtual memory are employed when processes exceed memory capacity, allowing execution of processes not entirely in memory. impTopics.title: Clustered Systems in Operating System Design: Concepts and Structures
impTopics.description: Clustered systems are similar to multiprocessor systems but involve multiple systems working together, often sharing storage via a storage-area network (SAN). These systems provide high-availability services that can survive failures, with asymmetric clustering having one machine in hot-standby mode and symmetric clustering having multiple nodes running applications while monitoring each other. Additionally, some clusters are designed for high-performance computing (HPC), requiring applications to be written for parallelization. Operating systems in clustered systems use multiprogramming to ensure efficiency by organizing jobs (code and data) so that the CPU always has one to execute, as a single user cannot keep the CPU and I/O devices busy at all times.
